note: Recorded 2026-11-03 11:18 with the live investigator (claude-code:sonnet) on a local instance. SYNTHETIC case: the data is generated for this demo.

steps.label: Read the report and earlier results

result.headline: Cold-morning HSA launch drew 232 A, past the BMS limit; pack sagged and the FR inverter tripped on undervoltage.
result.explanation: Probably a cold, low-SOC pack (DCL 150 A) sagging under the VCU 2.4.1 hill-start torque ramp, which exceeded the BMS limit. The FR inverter is the first to cross 55 V. FR-specific wiring is not excluded.

evidence.quote: VCU_TqDebug   TqReq_Base=69.1 TqHSA_FF=39.4 TqLim_BMS=80.2 TqCmd_Out=108.5 (N.m per wheel)
evidence.shows: HSA feed-forward adds to the base request. Output torque exceeds the BMS torque limit of 80.2 and reaches 125.2 at line 1416.

evidence.quote: BMS_Event     WARN discharge current 174 A above DCL 150 A
evidence.shows: First warning in the chain, 0.15 s before the inverter DTC. Current later reaches 232.1 A.

evidence.quote: MCU_FR_Event  ERROR DTC 0x2A11 DC bus under-voltage (54.3 V < 55.0 V for >= 50 ms), torque disabled
evidence.shows: The FR inverter trips on bus undervoltage as the pack sags to 55.85 V at 232.1 A. Cell 13 is at 2.664 V and cells are at 2-4 °C.

evidence.quote: MCU_FR        DC_V=54.37 Tq_Act=124.1 Spd_rpm=14 T_inv=6 DTC=0x0000
evidence.shows: FR reads lower than FL (55.45 V at line 1409) at the same instant, so it crosses the threshold first.

evidence.quote: BMS_Status    Pack_V=74.28 Pack_I=3.0 SOC=61 DCL_A=300 T_cell_min=18 T_cell_max=20 SOH=91
evidence.shows: In the afternoon the pack is warm with SOC 61 and DCL 300 A. TqLim_BMS is 161.7 and the same HSA ramp is capped at 132. No fault in that launch.

checked.result: Warning, then inverter DTC, then VCU fault, then e-stop. Pack voltage falls from 60.18 V (line 1386) to 55.85 V (line 1407) as current rises to 232.1 A.

checked.check: Time from BMS WARN to FR DTC
checked.result: One BMS warning, 0.15 s (30 lines) before MCU_FR_Event.
checked.about: Pack limit exceeded before the inverter trip

checked.check: Searched for event messages across the three snapshots
checked.result: The 10/09 launch (VCU 2.3.8, before the OTA) logs 'HSA not available'. The 10/28 launches log 'HSA enabled'. Only the morning launch has the BMS warning and the faults.

checked.check: Compared HSA feed-forward and BMS limit, morning vs afternoon
checked.result: Same HSA ramp (FF 45.0). The morning cap is 80.2 and the command reaches 125.2. The afternoon cap is 161.7 and the command is held at 132.
checked.about: Cold pack limit not applied to the HSA torque

checked.result: FR shows no DTC before its bus voltage drops (line 1410, DTC=0x0000). The other inverters track the same sag (FL 55.45 V). The controller was already replaced on 10/21 and the problem returned (line 4).

effects.quote: VCU_Event     ERROR FaultLevel=3 MotorFault_FR=1: torque cut on all wheels, EPB apply, Remote_Code=7
AD_Event      ERROR chassis fault reported by VCU -> EMERGENCY STOP, mission paused
effects.why: Autonomy response to the VCU fault.

effects.quote: MCU_FR        DC_V=58.75 Tq_Act=0.0 Spd_rpm=22 T_inv=6 DTC=0x2A11
effects.why: Torque is disabled, so the load drops and the voltage recovers (72.32 V by line 1440). This is not a separate fault.

next_action.action: Measure voltage at the FR inverter input versus the pack terminals during a loaded launch.
next_action.why: Separates a pack/VCU current problem from an FR-specific supply drop, since FR reads lower than FL on CAN.
how: Put a logger or meter on the pack terminals and at the FR and FL inverter DC inputs.
Run a B-ramp launch in the cold morning with HSA on.
Compare FR-to-pack drop against FL-to-pack drop at peak launch current.
Inspect the FR DC connector and busbar for heating or high resistance.

outcomes.label: FR drop clearly larger than FL
outcomes.means: FR supply path (connector or cable) adds resistance and makes FR trip first.
outcomes.then: Plan a repair of the FR supply path, then re-test the cold launch.

outcomes.label: Drops equal, pack itself sags below 55 V
outcomes.means: Pack sag under cold, low SOC, high current. The VCU does not honour the BMS limit.
outcomes.then: Propose a VCU HSA clamp to TqLim_BMS and a cold/SOC check.

outcomes.label: No fault and voltage stays above 55 V
outcomes.means: The condition is not reproduced. Try again with a colder, lower-SOC pack.
outcomes.then: Repeat at the next cold, low-SOC morning.

unknowns: Whether the VCU is meant to clamp HSA torque to TqLim_BMS, or whether the HSA feed-forward bypasses it.
Whether the earlier incidents on 10/20 and 10/21 had the same cold, low-SOC conditions (only 10/28 data is available).
Why FR reads lower than FL, RL and RR (wiring versus measurement offset).

hypotheses.claim: A cold, low-SOC pack with a 150 A discharge limit sags below 55 V under launch current.
hypotheses.because: Pack falls to 55.85 V at 232.1 A with cell 13 at 2.664 V and 2-4 °C. The warm afternoon launch has a 300 A limit and no fault.
hypotheses.observed_at: BMS_Status and MCU DC_V on chassis CAN

hypotheses.claim: HSA feed-forward pushes torque past the BMS torque limit, so current exceeds DCL.
hypotheses.because: TqCmd_Out reaches 125.2 against TqLim_BMS 80.2. The pre-OTA launch (2.3.8, no HSA) had no fault. Problems started after the 10/14 OTA.

hypotheses.claim: The FR inverter has a fault or a mis-set undervoltage threshold.
hypotheses.because: The inverter was replaced on 10/21 and the problem returned. The trip follows a real bus-voltage drop and the other inverters show the same trend.
hypotheses.observed_at: MCU_FR DC_V on CAN; the inverter was not tested directly

hypotheses.claim: High resistance in the FR supply path makes FR read the lowest bus voltage.
hypotheses.because: FR reads lower than FL throughout the ramp (54.37 V vs 55.45 V at line 1409-1410). The log cannot tell a wiring drop from a measurement offset.

events.what: HSA feed-forward raises torque command above the BMS limit
events.why: Torque ramps to 125.2 against TqLim_BMS 80.2 on the cold pack.

events.what: Pack voltage sags to 55.85 V; cell 13 at 2.664 V
events.why: Bus voltage nears the 55 V inverter threshold.

events.what: BMS warns discharge current above DCL
events.why: Earliest explicit warning, before the inverter trip.

events.what: FR bus voltage consistently below the other inverters

events.why: Result of the bus dropping below 55 V for 50 ms.
Normal start-up messages; they show HSA enabled only after the OTA.

result.lesson: No earlier cases are available for this signature.
result.reuse_when: Machines with VCU 2.4.1 hill-start assist on an NCM 20S pack that cold-start on grade with low SOC; log shows BMS WARN above DCL, then an inverter undervoltage DTC and VCU remote code 7.
